about: Tap-to-switch contract shared by all six front ends (Android app + tile, Omarchy popup, Mac menu bar, web dashboard, desk bar, couch). One tap on the device in hand moves the Bose there with a true status. Every front end's tests load this file and assert the same texts and outcomes. Roles in scenarios are abstract: 'here' is the device the tap happens on; 'other1' and 'other2' are the two other roles in the order phone, mac, pc with 'here' removed.

body.request_id: short random id from the front end (optional)
body.replace: address of the slot to drop (optional, only after a busy reply)

messages.busy: Both slots busy · choose one to replace

errors.unverified: The headphones didn’t confirm the switch
errors.keep_one: Can’t replace that one: keep a phone, PC or Mac connected
errors.no_audio: Connected, but no sound from the headphones
errors.audio_not_moved: Headphones connected, but PC audio didn’t switch

rules.pending_immediately: messages.pending shows at once on tap, before any reply
rules.retry: A connect that is not confirmed is retried (resent at most once after a fresh read shows the target absent and a slot free; on Linux the PC also pages BlueZ every 3 s for up to 45 s). Never resend through another peer while a reply is outstanding.
rules.both_busy: Never guess which slot to drop: reply busy with both slots; the front end offers messages.replace per slot; the chosen address goes back as replace
rules.verified: Success only after a fresh headset read shows 'here' connected; on Linux PC also the Bose A2DP sink is the default sink
rules.log: One line per switch request on the executing controller: 'bose.switch source={source} id={id} target={target_label} replace={label_or_-} outcome={ok|busy|error:<key>} via={local|peer:<id>} total={seconds:.2f}s'. Device role labels only, never addresses or names.
